practices: Assessments evaluate core understanding in Structure and Reactivity. Strict adherence to command terms: State, Outline, Describe, and Explain are the dominant cognitive targets. Calculations must show intermediate dimensional analysis steps.

keyTopics: Particulate nature of matter and physical changes
The nuclear atom, isotopes, nuclear symbols
Counting particles by mass: The mole, molar mass
The ionic model, crystal lattices, formula units
The covalent model, Lewis structures, coordinate bonds
Macromolecules (silicon dioxide, diamond) and metallic bonding
From models to real substances, electronegativity differences
Measuring energy changes in chemical reactions, calorimetry
Enthalpy changes, combustion, neutralization, Hess's Law

units.unitTitle: How much, how fast and how far?
keyTopics: Equilibrium law, Kc expression and basic calculations
Proton transfer reactions, strong acids and bases, pH scale
Electron transfer reactions, redox cells, oxidation states

antiPatterns: Avoid HL extension topics under all circumstances. Never ask questions about: transition metal ligand coordinate bonding shapes or color theories (S1.3), orbital hybridisation/sigma-pi bonding mechanisms (S2.2), entropy calculations/Gibbs free energy spontaneity (R1.2), energy cycles/Born-Haber cycles (R1.3), rate laws/mechanisms/differential rates (R2.2), weak acid buffer solutions/calculations (R3.1), electrolysis/Nernst equations (R3.2), and organic mechanisms (Sn1, Sn2, nucleophilic substitution) (R3.4). Keep questions qualitative and conceptual.
